nodes.summary: The dyadic approximants `2 ^ (-n) • f (2 ^ n • x)` used in Hyers' proof.
nodes.title: Dyadic approximants in Hyers' proof

nodes.summary: Two additive maps both within `δ` of the same `f` are equal: their difference is additive, hence `n`-homogeneous, while staying bounded by `2 * δ`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness in Hyers' theorem

nodes.summary: If `f : E → F` between real normed spaces, with `F` complete, satisfies `‖f (x + y) - f x - f y‖ ≤ δ` for all `x, y`, then there is an additive map `A : E →+ F` with `‖f x - A x‖ ≤ δ` for all `x`. The bound `δ` is sharp: for `f x = x + c` on `ℝ` the defect is `‖c‖` and the best additive approximant is the identity, at distance exactly `‖c‖`.
nodes.title: Hyers' theorem (Hyers–Ulam stability of the Cauchy equation)

nodes.summary: If the midpoint (Jensen) defect `‖f ((1/2) • (x + y)) - (1/2) • (f x + f y)‖` is `≤ δ` for all `x, y`, then `f` is within `4 * δ` of an additive map plus the constant `f 0`. The factor `4` comes from doubling the two Jensen estimates at `(x + y, 0)` and `(x, y)`.
nodes.title: Hyers–Ulam stability of Jensen's functional equation

nodes.summary: If `f` is continuous at `0` (in particular if `f` itself is continuous), the additive approximant from Hyers' theorem is continuous, hence a continuous real-linear map. The proof: continuity of `f` at `0` bounds `f` on a small ball, so the approximant is bounded on that ball, and an additive map bounded on a ball is continuous at `0` by the dyadic scaling argument.
nodes.title: Continuous Hyers–Ulam stability

nodes.summary: Norm of a natural-number multiple in a real normed space.
nodes.title: Norm of a natural-number multiple

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
